chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Hariz from Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan said:

A group of our companions performed Hajj, and when they arrived in Medina and visited Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), they said, 'Zurarah commanded us to perform Hajj al-Qiran (or combine Umrah and Hajj) when we entered the state of Ihram.' He said to them, 'Perform Hajj al-Tamattu'.' When they left his presence, I entered upon him and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, by God, if you do not inform them of what you informed Zurarah of, they will go to Kufa and be called liars there.' He said, 'Bring them back to me.' So they entered upon him, and he said, 'Zurarah has spoken the truth.' Then he said, 'By God, no one will hear this from me after today.'

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, the fourth Imam
key_terms.اَلْإِحْرَامُ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.اَلْكُوفَة: Kufa, a major city in Iraq and center of Shia scholarship
key_terms.تَمَتَّعُوا: Perform Hajj al-Tamattu' (separating Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.زُرَارَة: Zurarah ibn A'yan, a prominent companion of the Imams
key_terms.نُهِلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: To perform Hajj al-Qiran (combining Umrah and Hajj together)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Hajj al-Qiran and Hajj al-Tamattu' according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the principle of *al-tawassu* (flexibility) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam al-Baqir (AS) validates Zurarah’s instruction of *Qiran* while recommending *Tamattu'* for the companions, demonstrating that multiple valid practices can coexist under the Imam's authority. The Imam’s subsequent declaration that 'no one will hear this from me after today' underscores the dynamic nature of *fiqh* and the Imam's role in tailoring rulings to the specific circumstances and understanding of his followers. This incident serves as a foundational example of how the Imams clarified legal nuances to prevent confusion among the early Muslim community.
